pr.title: SCM - add `scm.diffDecorationsAlgorithm` setting
pr.body:
Since #249106 changed the diffing algorithm from `legacy` to `advanced` for the quick diff, the quick diff got quite slow for large files (>400 lines), often marking all the lines as "modified" even when `git status` shows nothing (#253704).

To workaround this, this PR adds a new setting `scm.diffDecorationsAlgorithm` for the diffing algorithm used for quick diff. The default value is `advanced`.

Co-authored-by: Codex

reviews.body:
## Pull request overview

Adds a new SCM setting to let users choose the diff algorithm used by Quick Diff (gutter decorations / peek view), addressing performance and correctness regressions reported after switching the default algorithm to `advanced`.

**Changes:**
- Registers a new setting: `scm.diffDecorationsAlgorithm` (`legacy` | `advanced`, default `advanced`).
- Updates Quick Diff’s model diff computation to use the configured algorithm (and recompute when it changes).
- Updates the Quick Diff peek diff editor to use the configured algorithm.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/scm.contribution.ts | Registers `scm.diffDecorationsAlgorithm` under the SCM configuration node. |
| src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/quickDiffWidget.ts | Reads `scm.diffDecorationsAlgorithm` to configure the embedded diff editor in the Quick Diff peek widget. |
| src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/quickDiffModel.ts | Uses `scm.diffDecorationsAlgorithm` when computing diffs and triggers recomputation when the setting changes. |
| src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/quickDiff.contribution.ts | Also registers `scm.diffDecorationsAlgorithm` under the SCM configuration node. |

@lszomoru Could you review this PR or at least assign a milestone? I really like the overall UX of VSCode, but #253704 is an intolerable regression introduced by #249106 in 1.101 that hugely degrades the editing experience and urgently demands a fix (or an option to avoid it like one proposed this PR).

If you already have another approach in mind for fixing this, I’m happy to close the PR. As an OSS maintainer myself, I also understand the hesitation around reviewing an AI-assisted PR from a first-time contributor.
